rules.rule: Check for urgent throat symptom conditions
rules.problem: Check task, trigger = sore throat / difficulty swallowing / painful swallowing as the reading of 'throat symptoms'. Every red-box item is present; BP < 90/60 is correctly left out as a routine vital. Only nit: 'red' dropped from 'Red swelling blocking airway'.

rules.rule: Assess throat symptoms not needing urgent attention
rules.problem: Trigger is Sore throat only, narrower than the page's 'throat symptoms' and than the sibling urgent task. A patient presenting with difficulty or painful swallowing but no sore throat (the typical oesophageal-candida presentation) never gets white patches checked for, so 'oesophageal candida likely' cannot fire for them. Otherwise the check_for faithfully covers every discriminating finding (bleeding and tender neck nodes are not used by any rule, so their omission is correct under the house constraints).

rules.rule: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from throat symptoms with sudden face/tongue swelling
rules.problem: 'check for anaphylaxis' correctly encoded as possible; structure (face/tongue swelling AND any-of list) matches the box; BP < 90/60 split into SBP < 90 OR DBP < 60 is correct. Allergen-exposure timing ('within the past few hours') is dropped.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable oesophageal candida from painful or difficult swallowing
Diagnose possible diphtheria from throat/nose pseudomembrane
rules.problem: 'Consider diphtheria' correctly possible; 'with or without mild fever' correctly left out. Plain 'Diphtheria' has no VHA name; the chosen concept is the general diphtheria concept (its did-you-mean), so it is right.

Structure exactly follows the flowchart: not the pseudomembrane branch, swollen tonsils AND (exudate OR no cough OR no runny nose). SNOMED has no bacterial pharyngotonsillitis; Bacterial tonsillitis is a child of both Tonsillitis and Infective pharyngitis, so it is the closest concept. The 'may also have' rash / strawberry tongue items are correctly treated as supportive, not required.

The (no swollen tonsils) OR (no exudate AND cough AND runny nose) block is the exact negation of the bacterial question, which is what the 'No' branch means. The extra requirement of red throat OR swollen tonsils comes from the descriptive box on the No branch; defensible, but it means a sore throat with neither recorded gets no diagnosis at all. Viral tonsillitis is a child of Viral pharyngitis and Tonsillitis, so the concept is fine.

rules.rule: Urgent: throat symptoms with danger signs
rules.problem: Urgent matches the box heading and 'Refer urgently'. Red-box items are all present and the anaphylaxis sub-group keeps the page's AND/any-of shape; 'Red swelling blocking airway' is sensibly ANDed as pharyngeal swelling + upper respiratory tract obstruction. The airway-obstruction item points to page 16 (airway); the house brief allows Emergency/'Very urgent' where a page escalates to airway, so a clinician may want that sub-criterion escalated, but Urgent is what the box says.

summary: Nothing on this page is invented or misplaced: every red-box item, every 'likely' diagnosis (probable) and every 'consider/check for' diagnosis (possible) is encoded in the right rule and role with existing SNOMED concepts, and the bacterial/viral split is the exact logical negation the flowchart draws. The one consequential gap is the non-urgent assess task triggering on Sore throat alone, so a patient with difficulty or painful swallowing but no sore throat is never checked for white patches and 'oesophageal candida likely' cannot fire for them. Minor imprecisions: the allergen footnote's 'within the past few hours' is dropped, and 'red' is dropped from 'Red swelling blocking airway'.
